Expected values of an mvgam model

Source: R/fitted.R
fitted.mvgam.Rd

Expected values E[Y | X] of an mvgam model, or its linear predictor with scale = "linear", at the training observations by default. The interface follows fitted.brmsfit().

Usage

# S3 method for class 'mvgam'
fitted(
  object,
  newdata = NULL,
  re_formula = NULL,
  scale = c("response", "linear"),
  components = c("response", "latent_state", "detection"),
  unit_level = NULL,
  resp = NULL,
  ndraws = NULL,
  draw_ids = NULL,
  summary = TRUE,
  robust = FALSE,
  probs = c(0.025, 0.975),
  process_error = FALSE,
  incl_autocor = is.null(newdata),
  allow_new_levels = FALSE,
  sample_new_levels = "uncertainty",
  ...
)

Arguments

object

An object of class mvgam.

newdata

Optional data frame with covariates for prediction. If NULL, uses original training data stored in the model object.

re_formula

Group-level terms to include: NULL (the default) for every one, NA for none. A formula choosing some of them is not supported.

scale

Character; one of "response" (default) or "linear". "response" returns expected values on the response scale via posterior_epred.mvgam(). "linear" returns the linear predictor on the link scale via posterior_linpred.mvgam(). Ignored when components is not "response".

components

Character; one of "response" (default), "latent_state", or "detection". The quantity to return:

  • "response": the expected value of each row of the data, on the scale scale sets.

  • "latent_state", for nmix() and occ() only: the latent state of each closure unit given its detections. That is the abundance N for nmix() and the probability of occupancy P(z = 1 | y) for occ(). predict.mvgam() returns the same with type = "latent_state".

  • "detection", for nmix() and occ() only: the detection probability of each visit, as type = "detection" of predict.mvgam() returns it.

The argument matches components of flocker::fitted_flocker().

unit_level

Logical or NULL (default). When TRUE for a closure-unit detection family and components = "response", sums the per-visit response matrix over the visits of each unit. Other components have fixed grains and ignore it. So do families that do not aggregate visits.

resp

Character specifying which response variable for multivariate models. NULL (default) returns predictions for all responses.

ndraws

Positive integer specifying number of posterior draws to use. NULL (default) uses all available draws.

draw_ids

Optional integer vector selecting a subset of posterior draw indices to use. NULL (default) uses all draws (subject to ndraws).

summary

Logical. If TRUE (the default), returns summary statistics. If FALSE, returns the full matrix of posterior draws.

robust

Logical. If FALSE (the default), uses mean and standard deviation for summaries. If TRUE, uses median and median absolute deviation (MAD).

probs

Numeric vector of probabilities for quantile computation. Default is c(0.025, 0.975) for 95% credible intervals.

process_error

Logical. FALSE, the default, leaves the trend's innovations out of the prediction. TRUE adds a random deviation at each time and series, drawn anew for every posterior draw from the spread the trend shows over the long run. For an AR(1) trend with innovation SD \(\sigma\) and coefficient \(\rho\) that spread has variance \(\sigma^2/(1-\rho^2)\). On a log link the deviations raise the average prediction by the factor \(\exp(\sigma^2/(2(1-\rho^2)))\). A random walk has no long-run spread. A ZMVN() trend has no dynamics. These two draw from the innovation covariance itself. CAR() draws from one long-run covariance at every time of an irregular grid. The argument applies under incl_autocor = FALSE. The fitted state already holds every innovation.

Each call draws new innovations. Two calls on one fit give different results. Set a seed to reproduce a result.

incl_autocor

Logical; whether the fitted values include the latent trend state the model inferred at each time. Defaults to TRUE for the training data, as in brms::fitted.brmsfit(). Defaults to FALSE with newdata. Under TRUE the observed response minus the fitted value is the ordinary residual of residuals.mvgam().

allow_new_levels

Logical; accepted for brms compatibility. A grouping level the model never saw is refused whatever this is set to. A new level has no fitted random effect. For a new series, it has no latent state to propagate. Predict for levels the fit knows, or refit with the new levels included.

sample_new_levels

Character; accepted for brms compatibility. It has no effect, because new levels are refused. See allow_new_levels.

...

Unused. Anything passed here is refused.

Value

With summary = FALSE, an [ndraws, nobs] matrix of draws. With summary = TRUE, a matrix with one row per observation and the columns:

  • Estimate: the posterior mean, or the median under robust = TRUE.

  • Est.Error: the posterior SD, or the MAD under robust = TRUE.

  • Q*: one quantile column per value of probs.

A multivariate model with resp = NULL gives a named list of these, one per response.

Details

As in brms, fitted values leave out the observation noise. posterior_predict.mvgam() adds it. Use predict.mvgam() for predictive draws.

For the training data the fitted values include the trend state the model inferred at each time. hindcast.mvgam() returns the same state. With newdata, or under incl_autocor = FALSE, the fitted values describe the covariate part of the model. process_error then sets the trend's part. FALSE keeps the trend's covariate effects. TRUE also samples a state per draw from the trend's dynamics.

The brms arguments dpar, nlpar and sort are refused. posterior_linpred.mvgam() returns a distributional parameter through its own dpar. Rows come back in the order of the frame.

See also

residuals.mvgam() compares the fitted values with the data. hindcast.mvgam() returns the fitted latent states. forecast.mvgam() predicts future times.

Other predictions: conditional_effects.mvgam(), conditional_smooths.mvgam(), hindcast.mvgam(), posterior_epred.mvgam(), posterior_linpred.mvgam(), posterior_predict.mvgam(), posterior_smooths.mvgam(), predict.mvgam(), predictive_error.mvgam(), predictive_interval.mvgam()

Examples

# \dontrun{
set.seed(13)
simdat <- sim_mvgam(family = poisson(), n_series = 1L,
                     n_timepoints = 120L, trend_model = AR())
mod <- mvgam(y ~ s(x, k = 5), trend_formula = ~ AR(p = 1),
              data    = simdat$data_train,
              family  = poisson(),
              chains  = 2, silent = 2)
#> Warning: 5 of 2000 (0.0%) transitions ended with a divergence.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.

# Expected counts at the training observations: the posterior mean,
# error and 95% interval of each
head(fitted(mod))
#>       Estimate Est.Error      Q2.5     Q97.5
#> [1,]  2.213963 0.9497584 0.8443745  4.477423
#> [2,] 12.868985 3.2440969 7.6262390 20.232959
#> [3,]  6.133415 1.8591295 3.1063965 10.225225
#> [4,]  4.267246 1.5377098 1.7451359  7.820154
#> [5,]  3.792407 1.4073015 1.6404318  7.154235
#> [6,]  5.103720 1.7479758 2.3529934  9.123604

# The covariate effects alone, without the inferred trend state
head(fitted(mod, incl_autocor = FALSE))
#>       Estimate Est.Error     Q2.5     Q97.5
#> [1,]  2.179257 0.4797681 1.370309  3.240618
#> [2,] 12.501430 2.3923246 8.346400 18.081087
#> [3,]  8.302232 1.3883129 5.749874 11.304569
#> [4,]  8.900367 1.6533494 6.174799 12.591126
#> [5,]  4.558828 1.0862699 2.787153  6.950084
#> [6,]  6.484566 1.7949456 3.705107 10.530367

# One row per posterior draw and one column per observation
dim(fitted(mod, summary = FALSE))
#> [1] 2000   90

# Next: residuals() and pp_check() compare the fit with the data
# }
